roadmap.title: TritonAI Roadmap
roadmap.description: A public, status-based view of the TritonAI ecosystem from the 2023 chatbot launch through the 2026 governed builder path. Recent milestones include initiative-level detail drawn from the public TritonAI Ecosystem Timeline and 2026 quarterly roadmap.
roadmap.source: TritonAI Ecosystem Timeline and AI Roadmap 2026 Q1-Q3 (presentation-test/ucsd-presentation, public-safe excerpts) and public product pages

items.title: Beta & Training
items.summary: Secured Chancellor's Office funding, invited 400+ staff to the campus beta, and launched AI Essentials I in the UC Learning Center.

items.title: Early Launch
items.summary: Began the phased rollout and launched the UC San Diego Assistant and Job Description Helper.

items.title: Campus-Wide
items.summary: Opened campus-wide availability for ~37K employees, upgraded to Llama 3 with campus SSO, and refreshed the UI with file upload.
items.source: TritonAI Ecosystem Timeline and TritonGPT release notes

items.title: Adoption
items.summary: Grew Fund Manager Coach adoption, expanded departmental use cases, and began infrastructure planning for the next platform phase.

items.title: Platform Prep
items.summary: Upgraded the platform architecture for scale and prepared the model gateway for both commercial and local LLMs.

items.title: Universal Access
items.summary: Onboarded 45K students, made GPT-4o and Llama 4 Scout the default models, and launched the 128K context window with My Documents.
items.source: TritonAI Ecosystem Timeline and public release notes

items.title: Widget & Infra
items.summary: Deployed the Blink AI widget without a login requirement and integrated LiteLLM to enable model choice.

items.title: Advanced Tools
items.summary: Launched AI-powered search and the Blink AI overview, expanded model choice for higher-value use cases, and began the Deep Research and chat UI refresh.
items.source: TritonAI Ecosystem Timeline and public release notes

items.title: Ecosystem Expansion
items.summary: Launched transcript OCR and student record matching, expanded instructional AI to 8 courses with scheduling assistant pilots, and opened the TritonAI site with API access and early N8N workflows.
details: Transcript verification moved from an OCR and matching proof of concept toward an OnBase handoff for enrollment operations.
Instructional AI added one-click assistant creation while scheduling and spring-course pilots continued.
Contract review expanded as a supervised Procurement workflow with configurable, policy-backed redlining.
The TritonAI site and Developer APIs opened governed model access for campus builders.
Research proposal risk and research alignment proofs of concept tested focused research-support workflows.
items.owner: TritonAI solutions team and sponsoring units
items.source: TritonAI Ecosystem Timeline and AI Roadmap 2026 — Quarter 1

items.title: Process Automation
items.summary: The builder path expanded, and TritonGPT moved into the campus mobile app. A Canvas-integrated instructional assistant shipped. Teams also advanced pilots in finance, transcript processing, and contract review. Research, BioBib, and observability pilots moved ahead as well.
details: Developer API access and N8N Agent Builder broadened the path from model access to supervised workflow orchestration.
TritonGPT extended into the campus mobile experience and began surfacing live campus signals with stronger response traceability.
A Canvas-integrated instructional assistant established a reusable delivery pattern for course support.
Transcript matching advanced toward admissions launch readiness while contract review added adjustable rule sets.
BioBib formatting, risk-based proposal review, and AI IT observability expanded the bounded prototype portfolio.
items.source: TritonAI Ecosystem Timeline and AI Roadmap 2026 — Quarter 2

items.title: Governed Builder Path
items.summary: Launching the TritonAI Harness pilot and initial hosted applications, organizing reusable skills and connector patterns, and preparing governance and observability for broader agentic development.
details: A bounded Citizen Developer pilot is testing a gateway-connected harness, tiered model access, and early project accountability patterns.
The TritonGPT Class Planner is moving through a supervised student rollout tied to registration readiness.
Campus App Hosting is beginning with limited-scope proof-of-concept apps and a shared-responsibility path to support.
The skills pipeline is organizing reusable UC San Diego skills, MCP integrations, and data-source patterns.
Shared knowledge work is testing reviewed promotion, source provenance, freshness checks, and scoped retrieval before context can be reused.
Academic advising remains in a scoped prototype and build phase.
Governance and observability work is documenting data, security, reliability, and operational requirements before broader access.
items.source: TritonAI Ecosystem Timeline, AI Roadmap 2026 — Quarter 3, and TritonAI memory architecture presentation

items.title: Governed agency at campus scale
items.summary: Evaluating repeatable, supervised agent workflows that can use approved tools and connectors while retaining accountable human review.
details: Agents would retrieve approved data and call approved tools only within bounded workflows.
Shared context would move from private task context to reviewed team or service knowledge through explicit promotion.
Human review would remain at consequential decisions and actions.
Observability would capture the reliability, usage, and evidence needed to operate services responsibly.
Successful pilots would graduate through a named service owner, governance review, support model, and approved hosting path.
items.owner: TritonAI program and campus governance partners
items.source: TritonAI strategy presentation and From Chat to Agents

source.description: Agent skills for UC San Diego and TritonAI

skills.name: tritonai-autoreview
skills.description: Use for TritonAI Harness or UCSD AI Tools code-review closeout before commit, pull request update, merge, release, or ship. Trigger when the user says use tritonai-autoreview, run TritonAI autoreview, autoreview this, auto review, Codex review, second-model review, review this branch, review this PR, review this commit, before merge, before ship, closeout review, run tests plus review, or fix accepted review findings.

skills.name: tritonai-feedback
skills.description: Use when a user wants to send feedback, bug reports, support requests, improvement ideas, or agent-experience notes to the TritonAI team. Trigger on explicit requests such as /tritonai, /feedback, /feed-back, /feed back, TritonAI feedback, email TritonAI, report this to TritonAI, or send this to tritonai@ucsd.edu.

skills.name: tritonai-harness-config
skills.description: Investigate and explain the live TritonAI Harness environment using sanitized runtime and source evidence. Use for Harness config files, CODEX_HOME or TRITONAI_HOME, permissions or sandbox modes, models and providers, skills, logs, installation paths, or comparisons with personal Codex or Codex Desktop. Also use for explicit T3 Code or t3code configuration/runtime questions, Harness-versus-T3 Code comparisons, or questions about a t3code identifier in a Harness diagnostic; not unrelated source-code mentions.

skills.name: ucsd-accessibility-compliance
skills.description: Use for UC San Diego digital accessibility work across websites, web apps, Campus CMS or Simple Sites pages, LMS content, forms, documents, PDFs, presentations, email campaigns, social posts, images, graphics, audio, and video. Helps implement, audit, or remediate content against official UCSD accessibility guidance, UCSD Digital Accessibility Standards, WCAG 2.1 AA expectations, ADA Title II and UC policy context, keyboard and screen-reader usability, semantic HTML, forms, contrast, alt text, captions, transcripts, accessible documents, and practical manual review steps. Trigger on /ucsd-accessibility, accessibility review, a11y, WCAG, ADA Title II, Siteimprove, screen reader, keyboard access, alt text, captions, transcripts, PDF remediation, or "is this accessible at UCSD".

skills.name: ucsd-branding
skills.description: Apply the UC San Diego Developer/Decorator 5 visual system to web pages. Use when asked to match UCSD/UC San Diego web branding, campus page chrome, current Decorator 5 documentation pages, or the components shown in the official Decorator 5 kitchen sink. This skill is intentionally limited to current developer.ucsd.edu sitemap pages plus the linked Decorator 5 kitchen-sink examples.

skills.name: ucsd-cms
skills.description: Use when authoring, editing, publishing, or reviewing content on a UC San Diego website running on Hannon Hill Cascade CMS (Blink, department sites, *.ucsd.edu sites managed in the campus CMS) — to follow the correct workflow, pick the right template/module, write valid metadata, meet accessibility and SEO requirements, and publish safely. Trigger when the user mentions Cascade, Blink, "the CMS", a `.ucsd.edu` page, templates, modules, drawers, tabs, metadata, display names, system names, SiteImprove, publish/unpublish, or asks "how do I add/edit/publish a page", "what template should I use", "why is my page not showing", "how do I get CMS access". Also /ucsd-cms.

skills.name: ucsd-data-classification
skills.description: Use when building or reviewing a UC San Diego application, automation, script, database, API, or data pipeline that stores, transmits, logs, or displays data — to classify that data under UC's IS-3 Protection Levels (P1–P4) and apply the handling controls each level requires. Trigger when defining data models or database schemas, choosing where to store data, writing logging, building forms or endpoints that collect personal/financial/health/student data, or whenever fields like SSN, credit card, PHI, FERPA student records, passwords, API keys, or other PII appear. Also /ucsd-data-classification, "classify this data", "what protection level", "can I store this", "is this allowed at UCSD".

skills.name: ucsd-memory
skills.description: Use and maintain an existing local TritonAI memory vault. Trigger on $memory, remember this, forget this, search memory, what do we know about, summarize this into memory, memory status, or requests to add, update, remove, query, or cite Obsidian-style TritonAI memory notes.

skills.name: ucsd-memory-create
skills.description: Create and maintain a local TritonAI memory vault. Use when a user asks for $memory-create, memory setup, an Obsidian-style memory graph, daily conversation sync, weekly memory cleanup, or cross-platform background memory jobs for TritonAI Harness.
